Unloading & manual handling of MS sheets/coils (Routine)
Manual lifting/carrying of heavy sheet metal; sharp/burred edges of sheets
Musculoskeletal injury (back/shoulder strain); cuts & lacerations to hands
Hand gloves, safety shoes issued; trained store personnel; edge de-burring at inward stage
Provide mechanical handling aids (hydraulic trolley/sheet lifter); edge-protection training refresher; team-lifting SOP for loads >20 kg
Forklift / hand-pallet-truck movement in store & yard (Routine)
Collision with pedestrians or racking; overturning on uneven surface
Struck-by injury to personnel; property damage
Mark pedestrian walkways; install convex mirrors at blind corners; reversing alarm/beacon on forklift; periodic refresher training
Shearing machine operation — cutting MS sheet to size (Routine)
Hand/finger entrapment at blade; sheet-edge cuts while feeding/removing material
Crush injury / amputation of fingers; lacerations
Fixed blade guard, two-hand operation switch, cut-resistant gloves (away from blade), trained operator
Verify interlock/guard functioning on periodic PM schedule; refresher training on safe feeding technique
Hand entrapment in punch/die area; ejected metal slug/chip
Crush injury to hand; eye injury from flying chip
Machine guarding, safety glasses, trained operator
Fixed polycarbonate chip guard at punch zone; mandatory face shield during operation; guard interlock verification
Continuous machine noise during punching cycles
Noise-level survey at operator position; enforce ear-plug/ear-muff use; consider acoustic enclosure if levels exceed 85 dB(A)
Direct/reflected laser beam exposure; fire from combustible residue; fume generation
Eye injury (retinal damage); burns; respiratory irritation; fire
Enclosed laser cabin with interlock, fume extraction system, trained operator
Verify cabin interlock function each shift; fume-extraction system efficiency test; assign trained Laser Safety focal point; keep fire extinguisher (CO2/DCP) at station
Hand/finger crush between punch and die during bending
Light curtain / two-hand control, guarding, trained operator
Daily functional check of light curtain before start of shift (checklist); operator refresher training; restrict bystanders from work zone
Arc / MIG welding of canopy & base-frame components (Routine)
Arc flash and UV/IR radiation exposure to eyes and skin
Welding helmet with auto-darkening filter, apron, gloves, welding screens between bays
PPE compliance spot-audit; ensure welding curtains maintained/replaced when damaged; awareness training on arc-flash hazard
Arc / MIG / gas welding — fume generation (Routine)
Inhalation of welding fume (metal oxides, ozone)
Respiratory irritation; long-term occupational lung disease
General shop ventilation; some local exhaust at select stations
Install/extend Local Exhaust Ventilation (LEV) at all welding stations; periodic workplace air-quality monitoring; respiratory PPE for confined/poorly-ventilated bays
Operation of welding machines / electrical connections (Routine)
Electric shock from damaged cables, poor earthing, wet conditions
Earthing of welding machines, periodic electrical inspection
Install RCCB/ELCB on welding power circuits; scheduled insulation/cable-condition checks; replace damaged cables immediately (do not repair with tape)
Welding near stored combustibles / packing material (Routine)
Sparks/spatter igniting nearby combustible material (packing, oil rags, powder coating area)
Fire extinguishers in shop, general housekeeping
Implement formal Hot Work Permit system; mandatory fire-watch during/after welding near combustibles; spark-containment screens; maintain minimum clearance from powder-coating/paint areas
Portable grinder use for deburring welds (Routine)
Abrasive wheel burst; flying particles; hand-arm vibration; noise
Eye injury; lacerations; hand-arm vibration syndrome (long-term); hearing loss
Wheel guard, face shield, gloves issued
Maintain Abrasive Wheel inspection register (mandatory record); rotate operators to limit vibration exposure duration; noise/vibration exposure assessment
Shot blasting of fabricated parts prior to pretreatment (Routine)
Airborne dust from blasting media; high noise levels; ricochet of blast media
Respiratory illness (pneumoconiosis if silica-containing media used); noise-induced hearing loss; eye/skin injury from ricochet
Enclosed blasting cabin, dust collector, PPE (respirator, ear muffs) per WI22

Verify dust-extraction system efficiency (differential pressure check) periodically; confirm blast media is non-silica (steel grit/shot) or provide additional respiratory protection if silica-based; annual audiometry & PFT for exposed workers
Handling/dipping of components in degreasing, acid-pickling & phosphating tanks (Routine)
Splash/contact with corrosive acid, alkali or phosphating chemicals; inhalation of vapours
Chemical burns to skin/eyes; respiratory irritation
Acid-resistant gloves, apron, face shield/goggles issued; MSDS available (per SOP-04)
Install and test emergency eyewash & safety shower at pretreatment line; refresher training on chemical handling; maintain spill-containment kit at the line
Working near pretreatment tank line — wet floor (Routine)
Slip and fall injury; secondary chemical contact from fall onto contaminated surface
Install anti-skid flooring/mats at tank line; enforce housekeeping schedule (mop/squeegee wet areas each shift)
Fume/vapour generation from heated pretreatment tanks (Routine)
Acidic/alkaline fume evolution from heated baths
Respiratory irritation to operators; air emission requiring MPCB compliance
Local exhaust ventilation over tanks; ETP for effluent (per legal register)
Verify LEV hood capture-velocity periodically; confirm exhaust routed through scrubber before discharge; cross-check with Environmental legal register (Air Act consent)
Combustible powder-dust cloud in booth; static electricity build-up; potential ignition source
Booth earthing/bonding, dust collection system, no open ignition sources permitted
Verify explosion-relief venting/panels are unobstructed; periodic static-electricity/earthing continuity test; strict "No Smoking / No Open Flame" enforcement with signage
Hot oven surfaces; possible LPG leak (if gas-fired); overheating
Scheduled testing of oven safety interlocks & temperature cut-off; LPG leak-detection check if gas-fired; hot-surface warning signage
Respirator fit-testing for booth operators; periodic health check-up for exposed workers
Liquid paint / solvent touch-up application (Routine / Non-Routine)
Flammable solvent vapours; VOC inhalation; contact dermatitis
Ventilated area, PPE (mask, gloves), fire extinguisher nearby (per WI38)
Use flameproof electrical fittings in the painting area; store solvents/paint in designated flammable-liquid cabinet away from ignition sources; periodic VOC exposure monitoring
Use of hand/power tools during assembly & foam cutting (Routine)
Cuts from cutting blades/knives; hand injury from power tools (per Assembly SOP)
Cut-resistant gloves, tool guards, trained operators (per SOP/ASSLY/01)
Periodic tool-guard inspection checklist; mandatory PPE compliance check before task start
Manual handling of canopy panels/components during assembly (Routine)
Lifting/carrying heavy or bulky fabricated panels
Musculoskeletal injury; crush injury if panel is dropped
Provide mechanical lifting aids (chain hoist/jib crane) for heavy panels; formal manual-handling training
Hydrostatic (bund) test of fabricated fuel tank with water — up to 1200 L (Routine, per SPEPR035)
Water spillage / slip hazard; structural failure of tank/weld joint under test pressure
Slip and fall; injury from sudden water release if tank fails; property damage
Written test procedure (SPEPR035), barricading of test area, PPE, tank placed on stable/level supports
Maintain a pressure/water-level monitoring log during test; define and mark drainage path for test water; periodic review of technician adherence to SPEPR035
Internal inspection/entry into fabricated fuel tank, if performed (Non-Routine)
Restricted entry/exit, potential oxygen deficiency or residual fumes inside tank shell
To be confirmed with Skyline whether internal tank entry is currently practiced

If internal entry is practiced: implement a formal Confined Space Entry Permit system, pre-entry gas testing, continuous ventilation, standby person and rescue plan. If not practiced, formally prohibit internal entry and state so in the SOP.
Air compressor operation for pneumatic tools & painting/blasting lines (Routine)
Entanglement in belt/moving parts; pressure-vessel rupture; high noise
Serious injury from entanglement; injury from vessel failure; hearing loss
Belt/flywheel guarding, periodic statutory pressure-vessel inspection, ear protection issued
Track statutory pressure-vessel test-certificate renewal in compliance calendar; acoustic enclosure/canopy for compressor to reduce noise at source
Electrical panel operation, maintenance & DG-set running (Routine)
Electric shock, arc flash, or fire from panels/wiring/DG set
Earthing provided, work carried out by licensed electrician
Implement formal Lock-Out-Tag-Out (LOTO) procedure for all electrical maintenance; periodic thermographic/electrical safety audit; arc-flash warning labels on panels
Overhead crane / chain-hoist use for heavy fabrication parts, if installed (Routine)
Load fall; struck-by suspended load; entanglement
To be confirmed whether an EOT crane/hoist is installed at Skyline; if yes — trained operator, visual pre-use check
Confirm crane/hoist inventory; obtain/track statutory load-test certificates; daily pre-use checklist; mark exclusion zone under suspended loads
Movement of forklifts/hand-trolleys within plant aisles (Routine)
Collision between MHE and pedestrians/racking at blind corners
Physical segregation (barriers/bollards) on high-traffic aisles; convex mirrors at blind corners; periodic MHE operator refresher
General shop-floor housekeeping — scrap, off-cuts, oil/chemical spills (Routine)
Cluttered walkways; oil/chemical spillage on floor
Periodic housekeeping; Safety Policy WI displayed at site
Formal 5S audit schedule with checklist; spill-response kit positioned at each high-risk work station
Fire risk across shop floor (combustible storage, hot work, electrical) (Routine)
Ignition of combustible material (packing, powder, solvent, scrap) from hot work or electrical fault
Fire extinguishers positioned across shop, Fire NOC maintained (per legal register)
Conduct fire drills at least half-yearly; appoint & train fire wardens per shift; display evacuation routes & assembly point signage; verify extinguisher/hydrant AMC records
Loading of finished canopies/generator enclosures onto trucks (Routine)
Struck-by reversing/moving truck; fall from truck bed/loading platform; manual handling strain
Struck-by injury; fall injury; musculoskeletal injury
PPE issued, informal ground-guide during loading
Formal wheel-chocking procedure before loading; edge protection/guard-rail at loading bay; trained banksman/signal person for every loading operation
Prolonged desk-based work — office & QA/administration staff (Routine)
Ergonomic assessment of office workstations; awareness on micro-breaks/posture
Use of electrical equipment / extension boards in office (Routine)
Eliminate temporary/loose wiring; scheduled electrical safety inspection of office area; portable fire extinguisher in office
Engagement of contract workers for maintenance/civil/housekeeping work (Non-Routine)
Contract workers unfamiliar with site-specific hazards; uncontrolled entry to hazardous areas
Injury to contract worker due to unfamiliarity with hazards; uncontrolled work near live processes
Informal briefing to contractors before work
Formal Contractor Safety Induction (mandatory before site entry); Permit-to-Work system for maintenance/hot work/height/confined space jobs; verify contractor's own EHS/PPE compliance & insurance
Site-wide emergency scenarios — fire, chemical spill, medical emergency (Non-Routine)
Escalation of an incident due to delayed/uncoordinated response

Conduct mock drills (fire, chemical spill, medical emergency) at planned intervals; maintain trained first-aider roster per shift; display emergency contact numbers & assembly point signage at all entrances
Cumulative occupational noise exposure across machine shop (shearing, punching, bending, shot blasting, compressor) (Routine)
Continuous/intermittent high noise levels across multiple work areas
Ear protection issued in high-noise zones
Plant-wide noise mapping/survey; mandatory hearing-protection zones with signage; annual audiometric testing for exposed workers
Heat exposure near curing oven, pretreatment tanks & shop floor in summer (Routine)
Elevated ambient/radiant heat near ovens and heated chemical tanks, compounded by seasonal temperature
Heat exhaustion / heat stress; reduced alertness
Provide rest breaks & drinking-water points near high-heat zones; awareness training on heat-stress symptoms, especially during summer months
Handling of gauges, weighing scales & measuring instruments (Routine)
Minor risk of instrument damage or minor hand strain during handling
Trained personnel, dedicated calibration area (per Calibration Schedule)
